newsitem.title: USA: McDonald's value plan to launch in 55 days.
newsitem.headline: McDonald's value plan to launch in 55 days.

text.p: McDonald's Corp said Friday it is ready to launch what it called an unprecedented promotion that will slash the price for some of its most popular sandwiches to 55 cents in 55 days and include a major new advertising campaign.

The fast food giant said its franchisees approved a national value meal programme that includes lowering the cost of some of its sandwiches to 55 cents when purchased along with a soft drink and french fries. The franchisees voted on the plan on Thursday.

"We're pleased that our owner/operators weighed the facts carefully and came to the same conclusion we did," Jack Greenberg, chairman of McDonald's USA, said. "This initiative will be good for our customers, our franchisees and our business."
McDonald's is apparently pulling out all of the stops for what's been described as its biggest national promotion ever.
"We're going to have a new ad campaign, new logo treatment and music," Brad Ball, senior vice president of marketing at McDonald's USA. "It's all part of what will break over the next 55 days."
Ball declined to estimate exactly how much the company will spend promoting the value plan, but he did say McDonald's will make "a significant investment" on the ad campaign.

McDonald's, which has more than 20,000 units worldwide and more than 12,000 restaurants in the United States, declined to confirm whether the Big Mac would be the first sandwich involved, as one franchisee told Reuters earlier this week.
A spokeswoman for the Oak Brook-based comapny cited competitive concerns.
The current price of the Big Mac, which varies from region to region, averages $1.95.
Industry analysts also said earlier this week the move could set off a price war among major fast food businesses, a conflict that could lower profits and harm relations with franchisees.
However, a spokesman for a group that manages advertising campaigns for the franchisees said the value meal programme could spark more business.
"We intend to attract customers with price and bring them back with the experience," George Kunz, chairman of the fast food chain's Operators National Advertising Board, said.
"We followed the due process, shared all of the information we had and asked for the collective thinking of our operators in helping to make a decision," Kunz said.
McDonald's stock fell 50 cents to $43.25 on the New York Stock Exchange.
